newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF panel wants to let banks to issue bonds.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF panel wants to let banks to issue bonds.

text.p: A key committee of the Ministry of Finance's (MOF) Financial System Council on Thursday decided to propose that Japanese banks be allowed to issue corporate bonds, the committee chairman told reporters.
Under the current law, long-term credit banks are allowed to issue bank debentures as a major means of raising funds. The law sets conditions under which credit banks can issue debentures.
Keimei Kaizuka, who heads the committee, said it also agreed to propose that banks not be allowed to issue a type of debentures now permitted for long-term credit banks.
The committee is expected to finalise its proposals on steps to deregulate financial markets next month.

The Financial System Research Council, which focuses on Japan's banking policy, is one of the advisory panels which Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto created to help set details of his "Big Bang" plans to liberalise the nation's financial markets by 2001.
"Committee members are of the opinion that it is strange that banks are not allowed to issue corporate bonds while ordinary companies can now issue bonds to raise funds," Kaizuka said.
The plan will help banks diversify ways to raise long-term funds when more banks are now offering long-term loans, Kaizuka said.
